## Description

A barrel-shaped ciliate (40–65 × 18–35 µm) armoured with plates of amorphous calcium carbonate, with
an apical mouth and three posterior spines. Omnivorous and histophagous: it eats algae and
flagellates and, in groups, injured or dead cells, which it tears apart in bites.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 6 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Histophagous](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md): it goes towards damaged cells (paralysed, trapped,
dying) and, if they are large, several eat them in bites. The three posterior spines are covering
processes (drawn only).

## Not implemented yet

- The carbonate armour is not modelled (the armour gene belongs to flagellates and amoebae).
- The species has not been validated against a measured growth rate.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Histophagy is unique to it; it exploits the [paralysis by toxicysts](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md)
of *Didinium*, *Dileptus* and *Litonotus*.
